source: Gill pasted these into the room on 23 Nov 2026. Verbatim. Do not edit.

sections.summary: A single lighting fixture shining warmth onto the concrete below, a weaving path, a lush understory, a tree canopy misted in the winter rain. The glow of a nearby cafes windows illuminates thoughtful human centred space. A covered area stepped back like an amphitheater, room for your gaze to rise up. I turn the everyday structure of a public space into an artwork that serves as both the primacy human level infrastructure and the natural eco system around it. Design that considered how it will exist from now and 1000 years into the future. When the installation is complete it’s as if it’s always been there and now it becomes a place that people want to come, to stay.
sections.describe:
I am Gill
I am James
I am an artist
a Cree voice rising

Picture an evening in Vancouver at dusk. One light, concrete, and nobody stops. Come back later. The same light falls on wood shaped by hand and on plants that belong here. Someone sits. Then someone else.

When the installation is finished it should feel like it was always there, but be a space people want to spend time in. A hub, a gathering place. It can be activated or left to rest. 

I make infrastructure as art, through an ethnobotanical lens. Seats, edges, light and plants, rooted in culture and made for people. The art has a job in the space, like the lighting does, and it's still art.

I add “invisible” elements too. By invisible I mean light, framing and composition in 3D space, the things that affect how folks feel and pull on the subconscious. Using planes, depth, and forced perspective in physical 3d space guide the human experience.

Imagining essential infrastructure as art and the basic human need for light & nature.

It's more than a stage, it’s imagining and considering how both the seer and the seen are considered. The audience gets places to settle, at different heights. 

The living part is art too. It can sit inside what's already growing, or become a new forest garden, made for what it will be in 100, 300 and 1,000 years. Using existing public space that through my treatment becomes a space to be. The Host Nations and plant knowledge keepers guide what grows here. Learning from them is an essential part of the work.

I'm looking for an underused spot in Vancouver with good bones. Some light already there, natural levels, a place to sit and watch. Perhaps interesting existing concrete foundations if natural setting integrated at street level but underused. I'll respect what's there and leave it improved, not overpowered. 

The form stays open, evolving. The site and the process decide. My vision, philosophy and guiding principles hold the whole way through.

Permanent impermanence

The making:
- Find the site and sort out permissions and insurance.
- Study the light there, day and night.
- Plan the planting with the right people.
- Mill my own wood and make test pieces.
- Build and install. A licensed electrician does any wiring. 
- Document it all on my own camera.

I have my tools and a workspace, may need access to wood and fab shops.
